title: The Gilded Oath Revisited
premise: Ada Coldharbour, a mercenary bound to the silent god Veyl and keeper of ledgers for the Gilded Oath guild—a brokerage of impossible trades, from stolen memories to borrowed years—has spent a decade keeping his head down and his oaths paid. When the old gods abruptly resume answering prayers, Veyl's silence is revealed not as abandonment but as imprisonment, and the thing that caged it wears the king's crown: a usurper feeding on divine power to march on the free cities. Ada's ledgers, it turns out, record every tithe the crown has stolen from the gods, making him both the key to Veyl's unbinding and the usurper's most wanted man. Torn between his oath to a god he resents, his love for guild archivist Sera Vane who is sworn to the crown's church, and his own hunger for the power he could claim, Ada ultimately burns the ledgers, unbinds Veyl at the cost of his own godhood-adjacent immortality, and frees the king—choosing mortal love and mortal justice over divine power as the usurper falls and the free cities stand.
about_author: Ansel Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing medieval debt records before turning to fiction, a career that left him convinced every ledger is a ghost story. He writes fantasy about bureaucracy, faith, and the people who keep the world's impossible accounts balanced.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ada Coldharbour audits a trade in the Gilded Oath's counting house: a fisherman selling his luck to a drowning merchant. Through Ada's POV we learn the guild's rules, Veyl's decade of silence, and Ada's quiet routine. Emotional beat: the comfort of order that we sense is about to shatter.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered in the Dark
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A dying guild courier's prayer to Veyl is suddenly, shockingly answered—the first divine response in ten years. The god speaks one word: 'Ledgers.' Ada hides the courier's body and lies to his guild superiors for the first time. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in longing.

chapters.title: Sera of the Crown's Church
chapters.summary: Sera Vane's POV. The crown's archivist discovers tithe-records vanishing from royal archives and suspects the Gilded Oath. Her investigation brings her to the guild under pretense of trade negotiation, forcing a charged reunion with Ada, her former lover. Emotional beat: love sharpened into suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Remembers
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Following Veyl's word, Ada decrypts the guild's oldest ledger and finds entries in his own dead master's hand: annual payments from the crown to an unnamed recipient—tithes of divinity. The king's coin has been buying godhood. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovery.

chapters.title: The Guild Takes Interest
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Oren Kell's POV. Kell learns what Ada has found and reveals the guild's true founding purpose: it was built to hide these ledgers from the crown. He orders Ada to bury the knowledge. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution that raised him.

chapters.title: Ashes on the King's Road
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The usurper's armies burn a free-city shrine; Sera witnesses a priest's prayer answered by a god that then screams. She realizes the crown is devouring gods, not serving them, and her faith fractures. Emotional beat: horror and the first crack in duty.

chapters.title: A Trade in Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada attempts to buy the truth of Veyl's imprisonment from a memory-broker within the guild. The price: a year of his life. He pays it and learns Veyl is caged beneath the capital's cathedral. Emotional beat: sacrifice as commitment.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Tithe
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV (the Crown-Thing wearing King Aldric). We see the entity's hunger, its slow consumption of the king's mind, and its discovery that a ledger recording its tithes survives. It dispatches inquisitors. Emotional beat: cold, patient menace.

chapters.title: Inquisitors at the Counting House
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The crown's inquisitors raid the guild. Kell trades Ada's location to save the guild's charter. Ada escapes with the master ledger but loses the counting house—and his only home. Emotional beat: exile, grief, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: The Road to Veyl's Grave
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, traveling with a smuggler caravan toward the capital. Veyl speaks in dreams, revealing fragments: the god chose silence to hide the ledgers' location from the Crown-Thing. Ada begins to understand his oath was a hiding place, not a leash. Emotional beat: reluctant reconciliation.

chapters.title: Where Duty and Love Collide
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Ordered to hunt Ada, Sera intercepts his caravan—but instead of arresting him, she demands to see the ledger. Reading the tithe entries, she defects, burning her church credentials. Emotional beat: love chosen over duty at real cost.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Refuse to Kneel
chapters.summary: Multi-POV interlude. The free cities' council debates surrender; Ada, arriving as a reluctant envoy, offers the ledger as proof the king is already dead in all but body. The cities agree to hold the walls if Ada can unbind the true king. Emotional beat: burden of leadership he never wanted.

chapters.title: A Year Spent, a Truth Bought
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The memory-broker's price comes due: Ada relives the year he paid away, recovering a suppressed memory—his master didn't die; the Crown-Thing consumed him, and Ada fled. His invisibility was cowardice. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Cathedral Below
chapters.summary: Ada and Sera infiltrate the capital through the guild's forgotten smuggler tunnels. They find the god-cage: Veyl bound in chains of ledger-paper, every tithe recorded in the master ledger serving as a lock. Emotional beat: awe and the terrible clarity of the plan.

chapters.title: The King Who Is Still There
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. They reach King Aldric, a flickering consciousness inside his own body. He begs not for rescue but for justice: he wants his usurper judged and the tithes returned to the people who prayed them. Emotional beat: pity becoming alliance.

chapters.title: The Price of Unbinding
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Veyl reveals the unbinding's cost: the ledger must be burned, and its keeper—Ada—loses the god's protection and the borrowed years that have kept him alive through old wounds. Sera begs him to find another way. Emotional beat: love against sacrifice.

chapters.title: What the Crown-Thing Offers
chapters.summary: The Crown-Thing captures Sera and offers Ada a bargain: the ledgers, godhood, and Sera's life, in exchange for becoming its new tithe-collector. Ada sees the corruption's full seduction—power that would let him fix everything. Emotional beat: temptation at its most persuasive.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Ledgers
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Ada refuses the bargain, ignites the master ledger in the cathedral's heart, and speaks the unbinding oath as the Crown-Thing tears the cathedral apart around them. Veyl's chains break. Emotional beat: defiant, costly choice.

chapters.title: A God Unbound, a King Restored
chapters.summary: Climax. Veyl, freed, does not smite the usurper—it drags the Crown-Thing before Aldric's restored body and the assembled free-city army, forcing judgment. The king, mortal again, passes sentence; the entity is unmade by witnessed justice, not force. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, made law.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Wounded, mortal, Ada wakes in the ruined cathedral. Veyl offers to restore him as its chosen; Ada declines, asking instead that the god answer ordinary prayers again. Veyl agrees and goes quiet—not absent, but listening. Emotional beat: peace after purpose.

chapters.title: A New Ledger, Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Ada and Sera return to the free cities, where the guild is reformed under new law: no more trades in what cannot be owned. Ada opens a new ledger and writes the first entry—a debt owed to Sera, to be repaid in years. Emotional beat: tender beginning.

chapters.title: The Gilded Oath, Revisited
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Ada's POV. Years later, an aging Ada teaches apprentice keepers the old ledgers' history, and a fisherman's answered prayer is ordinary news. On the last page of the first ledger, Ada finds his dead master's final line: 'The account is balanced.' Emotional beat: quiet, earned grace.
